subject: math
title: Probability: Impossible, Possible or Certain
seo_title: Grade 1 Probability Worksheets: Impossible, Possible or Certain (Free, with Answer Key)
standard_text: Use mathematical language, including the terms “impossible”, “possible”, and “certain”, to describe the likelihood of events happening, and use that likelihood to make predictions and informed decisions
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 math worksheets on probability for the Ontario curriculum: say if everyday events are impossible, possible or certain, find what you can land on with a spinner or pick from a bag of counters, predict which colour you will probably get, and solve short word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Certain means it must happen. Possible means it may happen. Impossible means it can never happen.
key_sub: If all the counters are red, red is certain. If some are red, red is possible. If none are red, red is impossible. The colour with more counters is the one you will probably pick.
body_html:
Three probability words

Some things we are sure about. Some things we are not sure about. We use three words.

WordMeaningExample
certainIt must happen.The sun will come up tomorrow.
possibleIt may happen, but we are not sure.It will snow today.
impossibleIt can never happen.A dog will drive the school bus.
Example

Our hockey team plays today. Will we win?

A team can win or lose. We are not sure.

Answer: Winning is possible.

Spinners

Look at the colours on the spinner. If all the parts are red, red is certain. If some parts are red, red is possible. If no parts are red, red is impossible.

Example

Is red certain on this spinner?

Most parts are red, but there is a blue part.

Answer: No. Red is possible, not certain.

Bags of counters

Look in the bag before you answer. You can only pick a colour that is in the bag.

Example

Can you pick blue?

There is 1 blue counter. It is in the bag.

Answer: Yes. Blue is possible.

Making predictions

When there is more of a colour, you will probably get that colour. If there is the same amount of each colour, it is the same for both.

Example

The bag has 5 red counters and 1 blue counter. Which colour will you probably pick?

There are more red counters than blue counters.

Answer: red

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Saying “certain” when it only happens a lotCertain means it must happen every time
Saying “impossible” when there is only a little of a colourIf it is there at all, it is possible
Not looking in the bagCheck which colours are in the bag first
Choosing your favourite colourCount the parts or counters of each colour
Thinking 6 is harder to roll than 1Every number on a number cube has the same chance

faq.q: What do Grade 1 students learn about probability in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario Mathematics Curriculum (2020), expectation D2.1, Grade 1 students use the words impossible, possible and certain to describe events. They use these words to make predictions and simple decisions, such as which colour they will probably pick.

faq.q: What is the difference between possible and certain?
faq.a: Certain means it must happen every time, like Tuesday coming after Monday. Possible means it may happen but we are not sure, like snow on a January day.

faq.q: How can I teach probability to a 6-year-old at home?
faq.a: Put some coloured blocks in a bag and ask “Is red impossible, possible or certain?” Then pick without looking to check, and change the blocks to try again.

faq.q: Why does my child say a colour is impossible when it is on the spinner?
faq.a: Many children think a small part can never be landed on. Spin a few times together and show that if a colour is there at all, it is possible.

sets.title: Everyday events: impossible, possible or certain?

items.q: The sun will come up tomorrow. Which word fits?
c: possible: it comes up a lot
items.e: The sun comes up every morning. It must happen. So it is certain.

items.q: A dog will drive the school bus. Which word fits?
c: possible: a dog can ride a bus
items.e: A dog can’t drive. It can never happen. So it is impossible.

items.q: It is January in Ottawa. It will snow today. Which word fits?
c: certain: it snows a lot in winter
items.e: It snows a lot in Ottawa in January. But some days it does not snow. So it is possible, not certain.

items.q: It is a hot July day at the beach. It will snow. Which word fits?
items.e: July at the beach is hot. Snow can’t fall on a hot summer day. So it is impossible.

items.q: Dark clouds are in the sky. It will rain. Which word fits?
items.e: Dark clouds often bring rain, but not always. So rain is possible, not certain.

items.q: Today is Monday. Tomorrow will be Tuesday. Which word fits?
c: impossible: it is not Tuesday now
items.e: Tuesday always comes after Monday. It must happen. So it is certain.

items.q: Maya is 6 today. Next year she will be 7. Which word fits?
items.e: Every year you get 1 year older. 6 + 1 = 7. So it is certain.

items.q: Our hockey team plays today. We will win. Which word fits?
items.e: A team can win or lose. Wanting to win does not make it sure. So it is possible.

items.q: At the park. Which is impossible?
c: You will go on the swings.
items.e: A tree can’t walk. That is impossible. The other things are possible.

items.q: At the park. Which is possible?
c: A dog will read a book.
You will see a Canada goose.
items.e: Canada geese live in many parks. You may see one, or not. So it is possible. The other things are impossible.

items.q: It is a school day. Which is impossible?
c: A fish will teach the class.
items.e: A fish can’t teach. That is impossible. Reading, recess and painting are possible.

items.q: It is a school day. Which is possible?
c: A cow will be your teacher.
items.e: Some days you have gym, some days you don’t. So it is possible. The others are impossible.

items.q: It is night. Which is certain?
c: You will see a shooting star.
items.e: The sky is dark every night. So that is certain. An owl or a shooting star is only possible.

items.q: It is night. Which is impossible?
items.e: The sun does not shine at night. That is impossible. The other things are possible.

items.q: Leah drops an egg. Which is certain?
c: The egg will turn into a chick.
items.e: When you let go, things always fall down. So it is certain. Mom seeing it is only possible.

items.q: A popsicle sits in the hot sun. Which is certain?
c: A bee will land on it.
It will turn into a toy.
items.e: The hot sun always melts ice. So it is certain. A bee is only possible.

items.q: It is a snow day. Which is possible?
c: A moose will drive a car.
It will be a hot day.
items.e: You may build a snowman, or you may not. So it is possible. The other things are impossible.

items.q: Owen says, “Rain tomorrow is certain.” Is he right?
items.e: We can’t be sure it will rain tomorrow. It may rain, or not. So rain is possible, not certain.

items.q: Zoe says, “Snow at the beach in July is possible.” Is she right?
items.e: July at the beach is hot. Snow can’t fall there. So it is impossible.

items.q: Kai says, “The sun coming up tomorrow is possible.” Is he right?
items.e: The sun comes up every morning. We are sure. So it is certain, not just possible.

sets.title: Spinners: can you land on red?

items.q: You spin once. Which is right?
items.e: All the parts are red. The arrow must land on red. So red is certain.

items.q: You spin once. Which is right?
items.e: Half is red and half is blue. The arrow can land on either one. So red is possible.

items.q: You spin once. Which is right?
items.e: There is no green part. The arrow can’t land on green. So green is impossible.

items.q: You spin once. Which is right?
items.e: Most parts are blue. But there is 1 red part. The arrow could land on red. So blue is possible, not certain.

items.q: You spin once. Which is right?
items.e: Every part is yellow. So yellow is certain. There is no blue.

items.q: You spin once. Which is right?
items.e: Only 1 part is red. But it is there, so the arrow can land on it. Red is possible, not impossible.

items.q: You spin once. Which is right?
items.e: The numbers are 1, 2, 3 and 4. There is no 5. So 5 is impossible.

items.q: You spin once. Which is right?
items.e: 4 is on the spinner, so 4 is possible. A big number is not harder to get.

items.q: You spin once. Which is right?
items.e: Every part has a 2. The arrow must land on 2. So 2 is certain.

items.q: Which colour is certain?
items.e: Every part is green. So green is certain.

items.q: Which colour is impossible?
items.e: The spinner has red, blue and yellow. There is no green. So green is impossible.

items.q: Which colour is impossible?
items.e: The spinner has green, purple and yellow. There is no red. So red is impossible.

items.q: Which number is impossible?
items.e: The numbers go from 1 to 6. There is no 7. So 7 is impossible.

items.q: On which spinner is red certain?
items.e: Spinner B is all red. It must land on red. Spinner D has a blue part, so red is only possible there.

items.q: On which spinner is red impossible?
items.e: Spinner D has no red part. So red is impossible. Spinner B has 1 red part, so red is possible.

items.q: On which spinner is red possible, but not certain?
items.e: Spinner D has red parts and blue parts. Red may come, or blue may come. On B red is certain. On A and C red is impossible.

items.q: Liam says, “Blue is certain.” Is he right?
items.e: Half the spinner is red. The arrow may land on red. So blue is possible, not certain. His favourite colour does not change the spinner.

items.q: Ava says, “Yellow is impossible. The part is small.” Is she right?
items.e: There is 1 yellow part. The arrow can land on it. So yellow is possible, not impossible.

items.q: You spin once. Which is right?
items.e: There is 1 yellow part out of 4. The arrow can land on it, or on another colour. So yellow is possible.

items.q: You spin once. Which is right?
items.e: Every part is purple. There is no green. So green is impossible.

sets.title: Bags of counters: can you pick red?

items.q: You pick one without looking. Which is right?
items.e: Every counter is red. So red is certain.

items.q: You pick one without looking. Which is right?
items.e: There are red and blue counters. You could pick either one. So blue is possible.

items.q: You pick one without looking. Which is right?
items.e: Look in the bag. There are red and yellow counters. There is no green. So green is impossible.

items.q: You pick one without looking. Which is right?
items.e: There is only 1 red counter. But it is in the bag, so you could pick it. Red is possible.

items.q: You pick one without looking. Which is right?
items.e: Most counters are green. But there is 1 red counter. So green is possible, not certain.

items.q: You pick one without looking. Which is right?
items.e: There are yellow and purple counters. You could pick a purple one. So yellow is possible.

items.q: Which colour is certain?
items.e: Every counter is yellow. So yellow is certain.

items.q: Which colour is impossible?
items.e: The bag has red, blue and yellow counters. There is no green. So green is impossible.

items.q: Which colour is impossible?
items.e: The bag has green, purple and blue. There is no red. So red is impossible. There is 1 blue, so blue is possible.

items.q: Maya wants a green counter. Can she get one?
c: Yes, if she shuts her eyes.
items.e: Look in the bag first. There are only red and blue counters. Green is impossible.

items.q: Kai wants a red counter. Can he get one?
items.e: There is 1 red counter in the bag. Kai could pick it. So red is possible.

items.q: Ava takes out all the blue counters. Then she picks one. Which is right?
items.e: After the blue counters come out, only red counters are left. So red is certain.

items.q: Noah puts 2 green counters in the bag. Then he picks one. Which is right?
items.e: Now the bag has red and green counters. So green is possible. Before, green was impossible.

items.q: In which bag is red certain?
items.e: Bag D has only red counters. So red is certain. Bag C has a yellow counter, so red is only possible there.

items.q: In which bag is blue impossible?
items.e: Bag B has yellow and green counters. There is no blue. So blue is impossible.

items.q: In which bag is yellow possible?
items.e: Only bag B has yellow counters, and it has red ones too. So yellow is possible in bag B.

items.q: Chloe says, “Red is certain. Red is my favourite.” Is she right?
items.e: The bag has blue counters too. Her favourite colour does not change what she picks. So red is possible, not certain.

items.q: You pick one without looking. Which is right?
items.e: There are 2 yellow counters. You could pick one, or a red or blue one. So yellow is possible.

items.q: Leah picks 2 counters. What is certain?
items.e: Every counter is red. Any 2 counters she picks will be red. So 2 red ones is certain.

items.q: Ethan wants a yellow counter. What can he do?
c: Put a yellow one in the bag.
items.e: There is no yellow in the bag, so yellow is impossible. Picking again or shaking does not help. He must put a yellow counter in.

sets.title: Predictions: which colour will you probably get?

items.q: Which colour will you probably get?
items.e: 3 parts are red. Only 1 part is blue. More red, so you will probably get red.

items.q: Which colour will you probably get?
items.e: 3 parts are yellow and 1 part is green. Yellow covers more, so you will probably get yellow.

items.q: Which colour will you probably get?
items.e: 2 parts are red and 2 parts are blue. The parts are the same size. So it is the same for both.

items.q: Which colour will you probably pick?
items.e: There are 6 blue counters and 2 red counters. More blue, so you will probably pick blue.

items.q: Which colour will you probably pick?
items.e: There are 6 green counters and only 2 yellow. More green, so you will probably pick green.

items.q: Which colour will you probably pick?
items.e: 3 red and 3 blue. The same number, so it is the same for both.

items.q: Which colour will you probably get?
items.e: 5 parts are green. Only 1 part is purple. So you will probably get green.

items.q: Which number will you probably get?
items.e: 3 parts have a 1. Only 1 part has a 2. So you will probably get 1.

items.q: Which will you probably get, 1 or 4?
items.e: 1 and 4 each have 1 part. The parts are the same size. So it is the same for both. A bigger number is not harder to get.

items.q: Which colour will you probably pick?
items.e: Count each colour: red 4, blue 2, yellow 1. Red has the most, so you will probably pick red.

items.q: Hana loves purple. Which colour will she probably get?
items.e: 3 parts are green and only 1 is purple. Her favourite colour does not change the spinner. She will probably get green.

items.q: Jayden wants blue. What will probably happen?
items.e: Look in the bag: 5 red and 1 blue. Wanting blue does not help. He will probably pick red.

items.q: You want red. Which spinner is best?
items.e: Spinner C has 3 red parts out of 4. That is the most red. On spinner D, red is impossible.

items.q: On which spinner is yellow hardest to get?
items.e: Spinner C has only 1 yellow part. The others have more yellow. So yellow is hardest to get on C.

items.q: You want blue. Which bag is best?
items.e: Each bag has 6 counters. Bag C has 5 blue counters. That is the most blue.

items.q: In which bag are red and blue the same?
items.e: Bag B has 3 red and 3 blue. The same number of each, so it is the same for both.

items.q: Mateo puts in 3 more red. Which colour will he probably pick now?
items.e: Red: 2 + 3 = 5. Blue: 2. 5 is more than 2, so he will probably pick red.

items.q: Kai spins 10 times. What will he probably see?
items.e: 3 parts are red and 1 is blue. Red comes up more often. So he will probably see more red than blue.

items.q: It is January in Winnipeg. What will the weather probably be?
items.e: Winnipeg is very cold in January. Snow is common. So cold and snowy is the best guess.

items.q: Dark clouds fill the sky. Should Noah take his umbrella?
c: No. It is not raining yet.
items.e: Dark clouds often bring rain, so rain is possible. Taking an umbrella is a good idea. Rain is not certain, so “certain” is the wrong reason.

items.q: You toss a coin. Which is right?
items.e: A coin can land on heads or tails. So heads is possible.

items.q: You toss a coin. What can you get?
items.e: A coin has 2 sides: heads and tails. It can land on either side.

items.q: You roll a number cube. Which number is impossible?
items.e: A number cube has 1 to 6 dots. There is no 7. So 7 is impossible.

items.q: You roll a number cube. Which is right?
items.e: 6 is on the cube. It may come up, or another number may. So 6 is possible.

items.q: You roll a number cube. What is certain?
items.e: Every face has 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 dots. One of them must come up. So that is certain.

items.q: Nathan says, “6 is impossible. It is a big number.” Is he right?
items.e: 6 is on 1 face, just like 1. So 6 is possible. Big numbers are not harder to roll.

items.q: Mei gets heads 3 times. She tosses again. Which is right?
items.e: A coin does not remember. Each toss, heads or tails can come up. So both are possible.

items.q: Before a soccer game, the referee tosses a coin. Our captain calls heads. Which is right?
items.e: The coin may land on heads, or on tails. So winning is possible. Both teams can’t win.

items.q: The teacher picks one name from the hat. Which is right?
items.e: Liam’s name is in the hat with 3 other names. So Liam is possible. Chloe’s name is not in the hat, so Chloe is impossible.

items.q: Chloe’s name is not in the hat. Which is right?
items.e: Only names in the hat can be picked. Chloe’s name is not there. So Chloe is impossible.

items.q: Only Owen’s name is in the hat. The teacher picks one. Which is right?
items.e: There is only one name in the hat. It must be Owen. So Owen is certain.

items.q: There are 4 red and 2 yellow popsicles. Emma takes one without looking. Which will she probably get?
items.e: There are 4 red and 2 yellow. More red, so she will probably get a red one. There are no green ones.

items.q: Only yellow popsicles are left. Liam takes one. Which is right?
items.e: Every popsicle left is yellow. So yellow is certain. Red is impossible.

items.q: Sofia picks a mitt from the bin without looking. Which is right?
items.e: There are red mitts and blue mitts. She could get either one. So red is possible. Green is impossible.

items.q: 6 children run a race on Sports Day. Ethan is one of them. Which is right?
items.e: Any of the 6 children could win. We can’t be sure it is Ethan. So Ethan winning is possible.

items.q: At the fall fair, the yellow ball wins a prize. Ava picks one ball without looking. Which is right?
items.e: There is 1 yellow ball. Ava could pick it, but there are lots of red ones too. So yellow is possible.

items.q: Arjun wins if he picks red. Which bag should he pick from?
items.e: Bag C has 4 red counters. That is the most red. In bag A, red is impossible.

items.q: Priya wins if she lands on blue. Which spinner should she use?
items.e: Spinner A is all blue. Blue is certain, so she will win. On spinner C, blue is impossible.

items.q: Benjamin needs a yellow counter for a game. What can he do?
c: Put a yellow one in the bag.
items.e: There is no yellow in the bag, so yellow is impossible. Picking again does not help. He must put a yellow counter in.

items.q: It is Canada Day. Which is certain?
items.e: July 2 always comes after July 1. So it is certain. Fireworks and rain are only possible. Christmas is in December, so that is impossible.
